_README: THE HOOK REEL. website/videos.html reads this file and pairs each entry
with its video in data/channel.json by id, so the thumbnail, title, link
and view count always come from the published record. This file carries
only what channel.json cannot: a one-line hook, and sometimes a tag.
LONG FORM ONLY, and no filter enforces it because none has to:
channel.json holds 69 videos and not one runs under ten minutes. The
shorts never entered that file. They live in data/thoughts.json, which
feeds the Thought of the Day page, and the owner confirmed on 2026-11-01
that each one clips and speeds up a long-form cut it came from. So the
reel, the wall and the carousel all show originals already.
VOICE. Each line works as a hook, not as a summary. It should make a
stranger want the video. The first pass read like a machine restating
each title back at itself; that got cut.
THE FOUR RULES THAT DO NOT BEND:
1. E-Prime, as everywhere in this repo. No is/are/was/were/be/been/
being/am. Note for whoever edits next: E-Prime carries NO legal
weight. It changes how a claim reads and nothing about whether it
defames. The protection comes from rules 2, 3 and 4.
2. The hook points at the argument, the pattern or the bit. Never at a
named person's conduct, health, money or state of mind. A title the
owner published ships under his channel; a line written HERE makes a
fresh assertion in the site's voice, which the site then carries.
Restate nothing a title alleges — let the title speak for itself.
3. Anything that ribs somebody carries tag: "Satire". The tag renders
beside the hook, on the entry itself, so a visitor who lands mid-page
meets the framing before the line. assets/videos.css explains why it
does not sit in the section intro alone.
4. The tag names the REGISTER, never the subject. "Satire" describes
how to read the video. It never describes the person in it.
Four of the ten rib somebody by name. The owner asked for them in on
2026-11-01 — they include the channel's most watched cut by a factor of
three — and asked that the framing name them as satire. Rules 2 to 4 are
how that got done.
Every line here got written for the site, from the video's published
title in channel.json and nothing else. None quotes the owner, none draws
on the private script repo, and none claims to carry a transcript.
Fields on an entry:
id    the eleven-character YouTube id. It must appear in channel.json,
or the page skips the entry.
hook  one line, in the site's voice, that makes a stranger curious.
tag   optional. The register to read it in. "Satire" where it ribs.
Order follows view count, most watched first. Keep the reel to ten.

entries.hook: The most watched thing on the channel: a satirical post-mortem on a brand that ate itself.
The cartoon villain nobody took seriously keeps making more sense every year. Uncomfortable, that.
Quantum entanglement, morphic resonance, and a ringed planet walk into one argument. None of them leaves alone.
Sixteen years on autopilot, then the lights came on. An account of waking up late.
A roast in the old internet tradition, aimed at an argument rather than at a soul. Take it in that spirit.
Forty minutes on Da'at, the sephirah the Tree counts but never numbers. A lurid title over a close reading.
The signs arrive early, loud, and almost comically on the nose. Most people file them under coincidence.
Less about one spectacle than about the mechanics underneath it: how a fall gathers speed.
A sequel, and a send-up of doom-posting as a way of life. The commentary voice at full tilt.
If the script already exists, what exactly do you think you decide? Free will takes a beating.
